content.title: What is Machine Learning?
content.explanation:
• Computers learn patterns from data.
• No fixed rules required.
• Learns by example.
• Finds hidden structures.
• Used for predictions.

content.title: AI vs ML vs Deep Learning
content.explanation:
• AI is the massive umbrella.
• ML is a subset of AI.
• Deep Learning is a subset of ML.

content.title: Types of Machine Learning
content.explanation:
• Supervised: Learns from labeled data.
• Unsupervised: Finds patterns in unlabeled data.
• Reinforcement: Learns by trial and error.

content.title: Supervised Learning
content.explanation:
• Uses historical labeled data.
• Learns the exact relationship.
• Needs an answer key.
• Predicts known outcomes.
• Example: House price prediction.

content.title: Unsupervised Learning
content.explanation:
• Uses raw, messy data.
• No answers provided.
• Finds hidden clusters.
• Explores the unknown automatically.
• Example: Customer grouping.

content.title: Reinforcement Learning
content.explanation:
• Agent in live environment.
• Makes random decisions.
• Gets reward or penalty.
• Learns optimal behavior.
• Example: Self-driving cars.

content.title: Why We Need All Three
content.explanation:
• Clear answers? Use Supervised.
• No labels? Use Unsupervised.
• Dynamic environment? Use Reinforcement.
• Pick the right tool.

content.title: Training vs Inference
content.explanation:
• Training: Heavy learning phase.
• Inference: Fast prediction phase.
• Train once.
• Run inference millions of times.

content.title: Data Classification Scenario
content.description: You have 10 years of purchase data. No labels exist. Group customers into 5 segments. What approach?

questions.question: Which algorithm to group thousands of unlabeled customers?
questions.explanation: No predefined labels means use Unsupervised Learning.

content.title: Lesson Summary
content.explanation:
• ML finds patterns from data.
• Supervised uses labels.
• Unsupervised groups unknown data.
• Reinforcement learns by interaction.
• Training learns, Inference predicts.
